distillation_scope_note: Disease-specific medical input is limited to the disease name: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Triggering antipsychotic class, dopamine agonist withdrawal, severity, serotonin-syndrome overlap, malignant catatonia mimicry, rhabdomyolysis, and organ-failure complications are represented only as axes, mechanisms, risk/context factors, event hazards, or treatment modifiers.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Central dopamine deficiency from receptor blockade or dopaminergic withdrawal
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Reduced dopaminergic signaling in hypothalamic, nigrostriatal, and limbic circuits after dopamine antagonist exposure, rapid dose escalation, depot persistence, interacting drugs, or abrupt withdrawal of dopaminergic therapy. This is the upstream driver linking the medication context to fever, rigidity, autonomic instability, and mental status change.

Dopamine-deficient hypothalamic thermoregulation, sustained muscle heat production, dehydration, and sympathetic activation raise core temperature and make fever less responsive to antipyretics alone.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Sustained skeletal muscle rigidity and contracture
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Nigrostriatal dopamine deficiency and peripheral calcium-handling stress produce lead-pipe rigidity, tremor, dysphagia, immobility, heat generation, myocyte injury, and rhabdomyolysis.
Central dysautonomia and physiologic stress cause tachycardia, tachypnea, labile blood pressure, diaphoresis, incontinence, arrhythmia vulnerability, and shock risk.

Dopaminergic disruption and systemic stress produce delirium, mutism, agitation, obtundation, catatonic features, seizure-like events, airway-protection failure, and diagnostic overlap with malignant catatonia.
Sustained muscle contracture, hyperthermia, dehydration, and immobility release CK, myoglobin, potassium, phosphate, AST, LDH, and tubular pigment load, creating AKI and electrolyte-event hazards.
Severe hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, immobility, dehydration, aspiration, seizures, and ICU exposures accumulate into DIC, arrhythmias, respiratory failure, shock, and death.

Ability to give oral or nasogastric dopaminergic medications such as bromocriptine or amantadine.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Fever and sympathetic activation raise pulse.
Hyperthermia and rigidity amplify muscle injury.
Sustained rigidity is a direct CK driver.
Myoglobin pigment nephropathy increases AKI risk.
Altered mental status impairs airway protection.
Aspiration can progress to respiratory failure.
AKI increases mortality through electrolyte, acid-base, and fluid complications.
DIC can produce clinically important bleeding.
DIC adds bleeding, thrombosis, and organ failure risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Stopping the ongoing antagonist removes the main driver.
Depot or long half-life drugs make offset slower.

side_effects.interpretation: Psychosis, agitation, or catatonia may re-emerge when antipsychotic therapy is stopped.

treatments.context_specific_role: Remove the causative dopamine antagonist driver while substituting safer psychiatric and supportive strategies.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Withdrawal-induced NMS responds to restoring dopaminergic tone.
Dopaminergic escalation can worsen psychosis or agitation.

side_effects.interpretation: Dopaminergic therapy can worsen tachycardia or orthostasis.
Hallucinations or agitation can worsen in susceptible patients.

treatments.context_specific_role: Restore dopaminergic tone when NMS physiology follows abrupt dopaminergic withdrawal.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Cooling directly lowers core temperature.
Cooling does not itself reverse dopamine-deficiency physiology.

push_targets.clinical_rationale: Cooling blankets, ice packs, evaporative cooling, and antipyretic support reduce measured temperature.

side_effects.interpretation: Shivering from cooling can worsen muscle activity unless controlled.

treatments.context_specific_role: Immediate temperature state support while causal and rigidity-directed treatment takes effect.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: High CK implies pigment nephropathy risk where hydration can protect kidney perfusion.
Cardiopulmonary disease limits safe fluid rate and may require ICU/renal support.

push_targets.clinical_rationale: Volume repletion improves renal perfusion and pigment clearance if urine output is recoverable.

side_effects.interpretation: Excess fluid can worsen pulmonary edema or oxygenation in vulnerable patients.

treatments.context_specific_role: Renal-protective state support for CK/myoglobin-driven AKI risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Benzodiazepines can improve catatonic and agitation components.
Sedation can worsen airway protection or ventilation without monitoring.

sigma_modulation.clinical_rationale: Sedation and catatonia control reduce physiologic volatility.

side_effects.interpretation: Respiratory depression risk rises with frailty or co-sedatives.

treatments.context_specific_role: Control agitation, catatonia overlap, and autonomic volatility while other therapies address dopamine deficiency and rigidity.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Dantrolene directly targets sustained skeletal muscle contraction.
Hepatotoxicity risk requires monitoring and may limit duration.

side_effects.interpretation: Therapeutic muscle relaxation can cause weakness.

treatments.context_specific_role: Reduce rigidity-driven heat and rhabdomyolysis, especially when hyperthermia and CK elevation are prominent.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Bromocriptine reverses the hypodopaminergic state.
Dopamine agonism can worsen psychosis or agitation.

treatments.context_specific_role: Dopamine agonist landscape reshaping for persistent or severe NMS physiology when enteral therapy is feasible.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Amantadine withdrawal can trigger NMS-like dopaminergic deficiency; restarting directly addresses that lane.
Amantadine requires renal dosing and can accumulate in renal impairment.

side_effects.interpretation: Confusion or hallucinations can worsen, especially with renal impairment.

treatments.context_specific_role: Dopaminergic support particularly relevant to amantadine or dopaminergic-withdrawal presentations, and sometimes used as an alternative to bromocriptine.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Dialysis rapidly treats refractory hyperkalemia.
Severe acidosis is a renal replacement indication.
Benefit depends on access to dialysis or CRRT.

treatments.context_specific_role: Organ support for AKI, refractory hyperkalemia, acidosis, uremia, or fluid overload while NMS drivers resolve.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Airway and ventilation support directly reduce hypoxemic death risk.
Telemetry and electrolyte rescue reduce catastrophic delay.

push_targets.clinical_rationale: Oxygen, airway protection, and ventilation improve oxygenation when failure is present.

sigma_modulation.clinical_rationale: Continuous monitoring and rescue reduce uncontrolled physiologic volatility.

side_effects.interpretation: Intubation and critical illness can introduce pneumonia risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Critical-care containment of airway, arrhythmia, shock, renal, and temperature complications.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: ECT can rapidly improve malignant catatonia/NMS overlap refractory to medications.
Anesthesia and ECT require cardiac and ICU readiness when arrhythmia risk is high.

side_effects.interpretation: Anesthesia and seizure induction require monitoring in unstable patients.

treatments.context_specific_role: Neuromodulatory rescue for refractory NMS with prominent catatonic or encephalopathic rigidity after medical therapy is insufficient.

risk_factors.clinical_rationale: Overlap should be preserved as context rather than deleted; it can coexist with or mimic NMS.

supportive_care: Immediately stop suspected dopamine antagonist exposure; if the syndrome follows dopaminergic withdrawal, restore the withdrawn dopaminergic therapy when clinically feasible.

Track temperature, heart rate, blood pressure lability, respiratory status, mental status, rigidity, urine output, CK, creatinine/BUN, potassium, bicarbonate, calcium, AST/ALT/LDH, WBC, and coagulation markers.
Use active cooling, hydration, electrolyte correction, and careful fluid balance; adjust strategy when heart failure, pulmonary edema, or oliguric AKI is present.
Escalate to ICU monitoring for severe hyperthermia, rigidity, altered consciousness, aspiration risk, respiratory failure, arrhythmia, shock, rapidly rising CK, AKI, hyperkalemia, or DIC concern.

Evaluate infection, serotonin syndrome, malignant catatonia, malignant hyperthermia, CNS infection, heat stroke, and toxicologic mimics as parallel context; preserve confirmatory exclusions outside ordinary ranking evidence when testing presentation-only diagnosis.
Avoid early rechallenge with dopamine antagonists; if psychiatric treatment is later necessary, wait for full resolution, choose lower-risk therapy, titrate slowly, and monitor closely.
